subject: Nucleus Labs — Eval → Reserve orchestration: GPU timeline & MAP
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Rivera <j.rivera@nucleuslabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nucleus Labs — Eval → Reserve orchestration: GPU timeline & MAP

Hi Jordan —

Following up from our call this morning. Per Nucleus's target launch window (early Q4) and the performance targets you shared, below is a pragmatic mutual action plan (MAP) draft that balances evaluation speed with procurement lead times for Dedicated vs Private deployments. I want to surface choices and risks so we can lock milestones at your side.

High-level sequence (proposal):
- Week 0–2: Evaluation sprint (set of 3 benchmarks + 2 production-like prompts) — Redwood provides a 1-week hosted eval environment and a gated dedicated pilot for throughput tests.
- Week 3–4: Pilot results review + MAP signoff — agree acceptance criteria (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, throughput).
- Week 5–8: Reserved capacity commit (if Dedicated) or Private onboarding kickoff (if Private/on-prem).
  - Dedicated lead time: ~4–6 weeks to provision initial tranche (dependent on region and GPU SKU).
  - Private lead time (VPC/on-prem): ~8–12 weeks for network & HSM/KMS setup + image certification.
- Tranching: start with 16 A100-equivalent GPUs and scale to 64 over 8–12 weeks (based on traffic gating).

Sizing assumptions (initial):
- Small pilot: 8 GPUs, 8k max concurrent tokens/sustained for model X-70B quantized.
- Production baseline: 16 GPUs reserved; automated burst to a shared pool for spiky peak.

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Private gives data isolation but adds 4–6 weeks to delivery and extra ops support.
- Committing to a Dedicated tranche earlier secures a lower monthly unit rate; late commits reduce guaranteed capacity.

I've attached a working MAP spreadsheet that maps milestones to owners and dates. Can you confirm the internal stakeholders on the Nucleus side (procurement and infra) so we can loop them into the DocuSign path once you sign?

Action requested from you: reply with target decision date (approve Dedicated vs Private) and any blackout weeks for provisioning.

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace — this is a helpful framework. A couple notes from our side after an internal sync: 

1) Timeline pressure — our product launch is fixed for 01-Nov-2027. We need the pilot completed and a reservation decision by 15-Jun-2027 to be comfortable. Is the sprint/pilot cadence you proposed compressible?
2) Procurement wants a clear list of deliverables tied to the MAP (SLA targets, rollback triggers, acceptance test details).
3) We need SOC2 evidence and a data handling summary for the Private option. Can you share the snapshot now?

Also adding some constraints: we prefer Dedicated for speed but will consider Private if there are contractual data residency requirements. Budget holder (Ethan) is CC'd — he will own commercial review.

Jordan
VP Product, Nucleus Labs
Procurement contact: procurement@nucleuslabs.ai

Subject: Re: Nucleus Labs — Eval → Reserve orchestration: GPU timeline & MAP

Jordan —

Quick technical sizing + lead time notes to give you more certainty. Quoting Grace's outline above.

Compressed schedule option (we can accelerate with tradeoffs):
- Eval sprint (hosted): 1 week (we run bench & kv/prefix cache tests).
- Pilot (dedicated) provisioned as a short-lived slice (4 GPUs) for ~2 weeks — fast path possible in 2–3 weeks if you accept a smaller tranche for validation.

Lead times (practical):
- Dedicated (reserved pool): 3–6 weeks for a first tranche depending on SKU/region and supply availability. If you commit to specific GPU family (e.g., H100x or A100x), lead time varies.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): 8–12 weeks (includes infra review, KMS integration, image sign-off).

Sizing recommendation for pilot→prod: start pilot 4 GPUs (smoke + perf), expand to 16 GPUs for baseline production reservation. If your traffic projections are conservative, 12 GPUs may suffice for month 1 with autoscale to 32 for month 2.

Notes on cost and performance: quantized model X reduces per-token compute ~1.6x but increases memory usage for KV cache — we should test a 3k token horizon in the sprint.

I'll attach a ballpark GPU-sizing workbook I used with similar customers. If Nucleus wants us to prioritize faster procurement, we can lock a tranche on our Dedicated inventory and bake a migration plan if you later opt for Private.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
